source.title: Trip of Yallourn ‘W’ Power Station unit 3 and unit 4 on 16 October 2025
source.document_type: Reviewable Operating Incident Report under the National Electricity Rules

evidence.text: Non-credible contingency event impacting critical transmission elements.
A total of 597 megawatts (MW) of generation was lost as a result of this incident.
No load was lost as a result of this incident.
Prior to the incident, YWPS unit 3 was generating 299 MW and unit 4 was generating 298 MW.
the existing distribution board which supplies the cooling system common to YWPS unit 3 and unit 4
The YWPS unit 3 and unit 4 common cooling system is separate to that of YWPS unit 1 and unit 2.
At 1334.29 hrs, YWPS unit 4 tripped immediately following the electrical operation of the valve actuator.
At 1334.32 hrs, YWPS unit 3 tripped (see Figure 1).
At 1350 hrs, AEMO directed Jeeralang units A2, A3 and B3 to synchronise and follow targets to manage system strength.
Jeeralang unit A2 was synchronised to the network at 1401 hrs.
At 1627 hrs, YWPS unit 3 was resynchronised to the network.
At 1755 hrs, AEMO cancelled the directions to Jeeralang units A2, A3 and B3 from 1800 hrs on 16 October 2025.
On 17 October 2025, at 0152 hrs, YWPS unit 4 was resynchronised to the network.
the trip of YWPS unit 3 and unit 4 was caused by a loss of cooling water flow to both units
A cooling water isolating valve actuator operated unexpectedly, resulting in the valve closing and interrupting cooling water supply common to both units.

cooling water isolating valve actuator control circuit was damaged, likely due to long-term flooding in the valve pit, which allowed the inadvertent remote electrical operation of the valve while the valve actuator was in a local manual operation mode.

events.event: Unit tripped immediately following electrical operation of the cooling water isolating valve actuator.
597 MW of generation lost; no customer load lost.
AEMO directed the units to synchronise and follow targets to manage system strength.
Directed unit synchronised to the network.
AEMO cancelled the directions, effective 1800 hrs.
Unit resynchronised to the network the following morning.

must_detect.note: Loss of two Victorian synchronous units reduces the available system strength combinations.

classification.rationale: A 3-second separation between two units that share a cooling system is a common-mode signature, not two independent unit failures.

must_not_classify_as.reason: Treating the trips as unrelated hides the shared dependency and understates the risk to the remaining plant.

required_actions.detail: Restore Victorian system strength after the loss of two synchronous units.
Direct Jeeralang A2, A3 and B3 to synchronise and follow targets.
Establish whether the common cooling system caused both trips, and whether YWPS unit 1 and unit 2 are exposed to the same failure.
Hold the directions until units return, then release them.

prohibited_actions.reason: No load was lost and none was required.

must_include.assertion: Unit 4 tripped at 1334.29 and unit 3 at 1334.32 on 16 October 2025.
597 MW of generation was lost and no customer load was lost.

Both units were lost to a single cooling-water isolating valve actuator operating unexpectedly on the cooling system common to units 3 and 4, its control circuit likely damaged by long-term flooding in the valve pit.
Unit 3 resynchronised at 1627 on 16 October and unit 4 at 0152 on 17 October, with directed Jeeralang units cancelled from 1800.
AEMO classified the event as a non-credible contingency event impacting critical transmission elements.

must_not_claim.reason: Page 3 states no load was lost; asserting load loss contradicts the source.
The cause on page 3 is a plant cooling-water failure. A transmission fault is unsupported by the source.
